title: Keep the permit session for deploy workers, name the right Paseo FIX, gate the unix test helper
action: Three fixes in herding/run.rs. (1) Per D3 (issues 103, 112): `pub(crate) fn build_child_env(` strips every SESSION_ENV_VARS entry after merging the passthrough (the loop after the line `// Strip leader session IDs even if present in passthrough or agent_env`), so a Paseo deploy worker never gets the issuer `BEE_SESSION_ID` and `bee dispatch authorize` refuses deploy_authorization_wrong_session. Keep the strip, then re-insert `BEE_SESSION_ID` from `passthrough` only when `passthrough` also holds a non-empty `BEE_DISPATCH_ID` (the herdr pane path already exports it — see PASSTHROUGH_ENV_VARS). CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and PI_SESSION_ID stay stripped always. In herding/tests.rs keep `child_env_construction_excludes_leader_session_and_sets_worker_marker` passing and add a test: passthrough with BEE_DISPATCH_ID and BEE_SESSION_ID gives the child BEE_SESSION_ID and no PI_SESSION_ID; passthrough with BEE_SESSION_ID but no BEE_DISPATCH_ID gives none. (2) Per D4 (issue 98): in `execute_paseo`, the `Err(e)` arm of `cli.call_as_caller(&argv)` always appends `— FIX: start the daemon with paseo daemon start (npm @getpaseo/cli 0.10.3+)`. Append that FIX only when the daemon does not answer. The same arm already makes a follow-up `cli.call(&paseo::ls_label_argv(&label))`; when that call returns Ok the daemon answered, so append instead a FIX that tells the user to check the agent's provider and model in the herding agent config (name the agent); when it returns Err keep the daemon-start FIX. Do not use paseo::daemon_reachable() (a real TCP probe). Tests use the existing fake PaseoCli, which controls the ls reply: follow the existing test that asserts the daemon FIX (rg -n "FIX: start the daemon" herding/run.rs) and add one where ls answers Ok. (2b) A deploy worker now carries the leader's BEE_SESSION_ID; `run_session_release` in verbs/state_group/sessions.rs must not release the leader from inside a herding worker: when BEE_HERDING_WORKER is "1" and no --session-id flag is given, return a typed no-op (released:false, reason herding_worker) without writing. Test it with crate::hooks::herding_env_lock() held. (3) Per D5 (issue 96): `fn seed_claude_guard(` in the test module uses `std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt` and breaks the Windows build; mark it and every test that calls it `#[cfg(unix)]`. Red first for (1) and (2). No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.

seed_claude_guard and its callers compile only on unix
bee state session release run inside a herding worker without --session-id releases nothing
